ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against FINTRAC PEP classifications as defined under the PCMLTFA, including family members and close associates; UN consolidated sanctions list; Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian sanction lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; and, because target payment rails include wire transfers and Wise, the United States OFAC SDN list is also applied in ordinary-course compliance. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any PEP, dual citizen, or cross-border relationship is identified. All screening results, source-of-funds explanations, and UBO identification records must be retained for at least 5 years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Service Alberta (online NUANS search and name reservation portal at alberta.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Roman/Latin characters under Alberta law; English and French legal suffixes are both acceptable. There is no mandatory translation into any non-Latin script. The corporate name must contain a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Corporation', 'Ltd.', 'Limited', 'Ltee', or 'Corporation'. Names that are defective, misleading, or confuse the identity of an existing corporation will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the initiating party must obtain the written rejection notice from the Alberta Corporate Registry or Corporations Canada, as applicable, and may submit a written administrative objection within 30 days of the rejection, providing corrected name evidence, additional NUANS search output, or withholding consent from affected similar names. If the objection is refused, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by originating application, subject to the court's requirements and applicable limitation periods. Federal incorporations follow the distinct appeal process under Section 12 of the Canada Business Corporations Act, with recourse to the Director and then the Federal Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For this offshore BIM/CAD outsourcing industry, a virtual office is acceptable only if it is a physical location in Alberta capable of receiving legal process and documents for service. Pure public-address virtual offices without service acceptance or maintained records are not permissible. The registered office address must be stated in the articles and filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry. The entity must demonstrate minimal commercial substance, including actual clients, payment activity, and operational records, commensurate with its Low_Risk_Standard banking tier.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; key sections: s.10 (incorporation), s.6 (articles), s.101 (registered office), s.8 (directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within the Government of Alberta Ministry of Technology and Innovation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Business Corporations Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; shares may be issued for any fair consideration. No escrow, capital deposit, or bank confirmation is required prior to incorporation. A single common share may be subscribed at nil cash value.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation is hereby ratified and adopted; that the issuance of one (1) common share to the sole subscribing shareholder is approved in consideration of fair value paid; that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [address], City of Calgary, Province of Alberta; that [name] is appointed sole Director and President; that [name] is appointed Secretary and Chief Financial Officer; that the corporate bank mandate authorizing wire-transferred receipt of client funds is approved; and that management is authorized to execute all registrations, including CRA Business Number and municipal licensing, incidental to the Corporation's operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS service providers or online Corporate Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request for the proposed 'Inc./Corp.' name. Ensure the search report shows no confusingly similar existing trademark or corporate name. A name reservation is valid for 90 days from issuance and must be quoted in the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in English and/or French
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion, select an alternative name from the NUANS report or obtain a written consent letter from the existing name holder; pay a new search fee and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 with the reserved name, Alberta registered office street address (no post-office box), share structure (e.g., unlimited class of common shares with voting rights), restriction on share transfers (optional), and statement of the first directors. At least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians. File electronically via the Corporate Registry online system or submit in person through a Registry Agent. Pay the statutory filing fee.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report and reservation number
Consent of first directors (acknowledgment of acting as director)
Registered office street address in Alberta
Name and address of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a Notice of Defective Filing, correct the flagged deficiency (name, director residency, or address) and re-file within the stated period; no material penalty if cured before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (certificate issuance) and Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation with the 4-digit Alberta corporation number, register with CRA using the Business Registration Online suite to obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN). As an office-based CAD/BIM outsourcing entity, you may request a GST/HST account (mandatory if annual taxable supply exceeds CAD 30,000) and optionally an import/export account for software licensing; no payroll account is needed if no Canadian employees are hired initially.
required_dossiers: Alberta corporate number and organization date
Details of signing officers and fiscal year end
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the BN application due to a registry data mismatch, verify the exact legal name and corporate number with Alberta Corporate Registry, then re-attempt BRO with a corrected confirmation number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting – Adopt Bylaws, Appoint Officers, Fix Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate action by sole director/incorporator; no governmental filing for ordinary resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of the sole director. Adopt the initial bylaw (Form 10 – By-Laws) governing director meetings, share transfers, indemnity, and fiscal year; approve the registered office (already stated in the Articles) and the first corporate bank account with wire transfer capability; issue the founder share certificates; appoint the President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer; authorize service providers such as registered agent or accounting firm.
required_dossiers: Directors' and officers' declarations (residency and consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bylaw provisions conflict with the ABCA, amend the bylaw by board resolution and rescind the defective provision; correct the minute book to reflect proper share issuance consideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Supplementary Alberta Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary (or local municipal authority), Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta, and Alberta Registries for annual return obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a physical office or service address is established in an Alberta municipality, apply for a municipal business licence; zoning must permit administrative/technical office use. If the entity later hires employees, register with the Workers' Compensation Board and open a CRA payroll account. File the Alberta corporate annual return (Corporate Registry Annual Return) within 60 days of each anniversary; file the federal T2 corporate income tax return annually.
required_dossiers: Lease or premises authorization for zoning verification
Website/contract details if required for home-based business endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal application is queried due to zoning classification, submit a landlord zoning certificate or apply for a minor variance; for late annual returns, pay the reinstatement fee and file the return immediately to avoid dissolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – office-based BIM and structural drafting services are outside the regulated practice of professional engineering under the Engineering, Geological and Geophysical Professions Act (APEGA). APEGA licensure is required only if the entity stamps or seals engineering documents under the Act; pure CAD/BIM outsourcing does not trigger a provincial industrial license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for statutory incorporation of a CAD/BIM service entity; a standard municipal business licence may be required solely for physical premises within Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 0 administrative/office occupancy: no EIA registration, approval, or screening under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 is required for paperless CAD/BIM operations with no manufacturing, water take, or emissions source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC discharge is generated. Office solid waste must be diverted per municipal recycling bylaws, and e-waste (servers, workstations) must be handled under the Alberta Recycling Regulation (electronic waste); comply with Alberta OHS Code ventilation and noise limits for office equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and clearance from the local fire authority per the Alberta Fire Code for office occupancy; structural load inspections are not triggered for ordinary commercial office use; workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act for ergonomic workstations and emergency egress; business interruption and cyber-liability insurance are strongly recommended for BIM data continuity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is the competent federal tax authority, operating the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business/register.html. In Alberta, provincial corporate income tax is administered on behalf of Alberta by the CRA under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement; the provincial fiscal authority is Alberta Finance – Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) (https://www.alberta.ca/tax-and-revenue-administration). Alberta levies no provincial sales tax and no harmonized sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an Alberta business corporation obtains a statutory tax identification number through the following procedure: (1) incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) via Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre or Alberta Corporate Registry, obtaining a nine-digit Business Number (BN) upon initial CRA registration; (2) where the BN is not obtained at incorporation, apply online through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO), by paper Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number (BN)', or by telephone; (3) open CRA Program Accounts necessary for the corporation's operations: Corporate Income Tax (RC account ending in C), Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) (RT), Payroll (RP) where employees are engaged, and Import/Export (RM/RD) where physical goods are cleared; (4) a non-resident foreign corporation making taxable supplies in Canada must separately apply for GST/HST registration using Form RC4155 'Application for Registration of a Non-Resident Organization for GST/HST (Simplified)' or BRO, and may optionally register for a BN program account without incorporating; (5) the CRA issues the BN in writing (Business Number confirmation / GST/HST account notice); the BN serves as the single TIN for both corporate income tax and GST/HST, and Alberta corporate tax is assessed under the same BN through the federal collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no U.S.-style 'check-the-box' entity classification election; a corporation is statutorily taxable at the entity level, and the CRA does not permit transparent treatment. Cross-border and group elections relevant to an offshore BIM/CAD export structure include: (a) Excise Tax Act (ETA) subsection 273(1) election for closely related corporations to treat certain supplies as made for nil consideration, eliminating GST/HST compliance friction between related GST registrants; (b) ETA subsection 167(1) joint election to use the 'tax charged in error' recovery procedure; (c) Income Tax Act (ITA) subsections 216(1) and 217 elections for non-resident taxpayers to compute Canadian-source rental/employment income on a net basis; (d) ITA subsection 219(4) election in respect of non-resident-owned investment corporation dispositions; (e) ITA subsection 250(1) deemed residence and branch-loss streaming allowances; (f) hybrid mismatch rules: Canada enacted targeted OECD BEPS Action 2 rules (ITA sections 12.6, 18.2, 18.3, 20(1)(n.1), 163.1 and 212.3) disallowing deductions in hybrid mismatch arrangements, but there is no elective regime—compliance is mandatory and fact-based. The Canadian corporation may also elect, under ITA subsection 249.1, an alternative corporate taxation year-end (other than December 31) with CRA acceptance, and a foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada may elect under ETA section 266 to be deemed registered in limited supply situations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) pursuant to the Excise Tax Act (ETA) — federal value-added tax at 5.0% in Alberta; Alberta has no provincial retail sales tax/PST and no HST (the 13%/15% HST regimes apply only in participating provinces such as Ontario and New Brunswick). BIM/CAD export services supplied from Alberta are subject to the GST regime, not to any Alberta provincial indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold under ETA subsection 148(1): a person, including a non-resident corporation, must register for GST/HST if its total annual gross revenue from taxable supplies exceeds CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the four consecutive calendar quarters; below this threshold registration is voluntary. A non-resident making no taxable supplies in Canada that only zero-exports services may apply for a GST/HST rebate of input tax credits via Form GST66 and may be registered on a voluntary basis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not presently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based continuous transaction controls (CTC), or digital stamping/e-invoicing for GST. CRA requires taxpayers to maintain adequate books and records in electronic or paper form (ETA section 286); electronic invoices are acceptable, but there is no mandatory e-invoice issuance or exchange platform. The Pan-Canadian B2B e-invoicing framework is nascent and voluntary, with federal, provincial and municipal governments progressively adopting Peppol/PINT standards for B2G invoicing; mandatory B2B clearance is not legislated as of the knowledge cutoff. For an export-service business, invoices should nevertheless conform to ETA section 169 input tax credit disclosure requirements (e.g., supplier name, BN/RT, amount of tax, description, date) and the customer's document retention rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 7, a supply of a service is zero-rated (0% GST) if the supply is made to a non-resident person and the service is not performed on tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance, is not in respect of real property situated in Canada, is not related to the non-resident's Canadian business or Canadian invitation/inducement, and the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST. For offshore BIM/CAD and structural drafting services supplied by an Alberta corporation to non-resident construction/EPC clients, the services will qualify for zero-rating where the deliverables (CAD files, BIM models, structural calculations) are produced for projects physically located outside Canada and the foreign client has no Canadian GST registry. Strictly domestic-to-domestic B2B supplies in the EPC chain (e.g., supply by the Canadian corporation to a Canadian prime contractor that later exports construction services) remain taxable at 5% GST. Services supplied to a non-resident that involve Canadian real property or the non-resident's Canadian establishment are taxable; therefore the Canadian supplier must obtain and document the client's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: No Canadian Customs export declaration is required for exported intangible/zero-rated BIM/CAD services; Canada does not treat engineering services as goods subject to export declarations under the Customs Act or the Export of Goods Regulations
Signed supply/services agreement with the non-resident client containing a non-Canadian project situs clause, delivery terms and payment currency
Tax invoice/commercial invoice referencing the GST/HST registration number and showing zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI Part V section 7
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103/MT202 wire transfer confirmation or Wise transaction receipt showing foreign-funder remittance to the Canadian corporate account
BIM/CAD deliverable handover records (electronic transmittal logs, issue sheets, PDF/IFC model download records) proving services are not connected with real or tangible property in Canada
Certificate of non-resident status of the client (foreign tax registration, registered office address, or client representation letter)
CRA Form GST66 (where applicable) claiming a GST/HST rebate of Canada-input tax paid by a non-resident, together with supporting invoices for Canadian input tax credits
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rated export claims under the ETA with heightened scrutiny on non-resident status, place-of-supply situs and the absence of Canadian real-property linkage. If zero-rating is denied, the supplier is assessed for 5% GST on the gross consideration together with daily compound interest under ETA section 280. Penalties include: (a) failure to register (ETA section 280(1)(a)); (b) knowingly making a false statement — minimum CAD 250 and up to 10% of the net tax amount (ETA section 285); (c) gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated net tax (ETA section 285.1); and (d) under the Income Tax Act, a false-statement penalty of 50% of the tax avoided for knowingly participating in a misstatement (ITA subsection 163(2)). Criminal prosecution under ITA section 239 and ETA section 328 carries, upon indictment, a fine up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment of up to five years, with additional civil assessments and potential revocation of corporate registrations. Under audit, repayment of claimed input tax credits attributed to zero-rated export supplies plus clawback interest is a standard consequence where the mandatory substantiation package cannot be produced.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary policy); foreign exchange oversight exercised exclusively under the authority of the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada maintains no designated central bank foreign exchange control body under a fully liberalized OECD capital movement regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions under the OECD Codes of Liberalisation. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, unpaid loan servicing, and capital repatriation are not subject to prior exchange-control approval, provided all applicable corporate, tax, and AML/KYC documentation is in place. No Canadian foreign-exchange restriction or central bank monetization requirement applies. Banking counterparties will independently apply FINTRAC wire-reporting thresholds and OFSI/OSFI prudential checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio in Canada. Contractors and corporate groups may retain export receipts in any freely convertible currency. For balance-of-payments statistics, Statistics Canada requires periodic reporting of cross-border payments, but no timeline or percentage-based conversion obligation exists. For the BIM/CAD engineering services exporter, invoicing in CAD or USD is purely commercial and unrestricted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account CAD and USD parallel accounts
Operational Account and FX hedging account
Operational Account and trade settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for regulated financial technology and authorized electronic money institutions such as Wise and similar cross-border neo-banks. Legal constraints: such firms must be registered as money services businesses (MSB) with FINTRAC, maintain telecom authorization or international money transfer authority, and are prohibited from offering deposit-taking products or issuing commercial credit. The primary treasury and operating account should remain with a Schedule I Canadian bank to minimize settlement and regulatory risk, while EMI rails can serve as collateral payment channels for smaller vendor payments and efficiency-oriented disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not mandated for Canadian corporate account opening. Remote authorization, document certification, and video-based identity verification are accepted under the bank's AML/KYC protocol when the entity is validly incorporated and registered under the Alberta Business Corporations Act or the Canada Business Corporations Act. The non-resident parent entity may be subject to enhanced due diligence, but a properly documented board resolution, certified corporate registers, and the appointment of an Alberta resident signing officer enable full remote onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Extended-reality engineering conglomerate with high cross-border invoice volume and a non-resident parent entity, triggering beneficial ownership and source-of-wealth review under Canada's Corporate Transparency and Registry Act (C-42/C-19).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide CBCA or ABBCA certificate of good standing, current certified register of directors and shareholders, beneficial ownership waterfall declaration, share-purchase agreement showing paid-up capital, audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years, transfer pricing master file and Form T106 detailing intercompany service remuneration, and the BIM/CAD outsourcing master agreement with project scope and billing terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious routing through digital EMIs or recurring constant cash-rounding where the purpose code is ambiguous, triggering suspicious transaction report (STR) requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full commercial invoice and the underlying work-product evidence such as BIM model metadata, 2D/3D drafting extracts, project acceptance certificate, time-sheet breakdown, and a payment schedule reconciling each email to the contract milestone. The AML defense must show that the invoice is for engineering services, not for capital flow evasion, and that all funds moving through Wise are mirrored by a matching SWIFT MT103 fee-line in a regulated bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low nominal share capital and potential circular funding identified by the bank's credit and AML analytics, especially when the Alberta entity acts largely as the parent's central procurement node.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the board resolution authorizing account opening, the contribution letter and incoming SWIFT record of the share-capital injection, executed sub-contracting agreements with engineering software vendors, occupied-registered-office lease, payroll and HST/GST filing confirmation, and a three-year financial projection proving economic substance beyond the conduit transaction. The entity must show its own risk management, billing capacity, and independent decision-making to avoid the bank classifying it as a shell or pass-through.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection from the non-resident parent requires a direct SWIFT MT103 wire from the parent's authorized bank to the Alberta entity's designated CAD operational account. The wire must reference purpose code 'FDI injection — paid-in share capital' under the Canadian Department of Finance balance-of-payments classification (category 'Direct Investment — Capital injected into a Canadian enterprise'); alternate bank credit notes must explicitly state 'corporate capital contribution' to prevent misclassification as factoring or commercial credit. Final verification includes matching the bank advice against a shareholder capital-contribution ledger, the board minutes approving the contribution, and confirmation of exemption or notification under the Investment Canada Act if the entity's asset value remains below the review threshold. For RMB or USD injections, the converting bank handles CAD conversion without need for central-bank approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational payments such as local payroll, office lease, and Canadian software subscriptions use the domestic CCD (Canadian Credit Clearment) EFT rail or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) with CAD settlement in less than one business day. Cross-border settlements for engineering procurement, royalties, dividends, and parent-company subcontracting are cleared via the SWIFT network using MT103 for direct beneficiary transfers and MT202 COVER for correspondent-bank bypass structures. Commercial documentary credits (letters of credit) are reserved for high-value supply contracts of BIM software platforms or specialty graphic workstations; these LCs must conform to UCP600 and SWIFT MT700/MT750 with full transport, invoicing, insurance, and acceptance certificate compliance. Payment purpose codes, when required, must align with Canada's T076/T077 (Balance of Payments) classification for 'Engineering and technical services'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forwards executed with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA or CSA agreement
Non-deliverable CAD/USD forwards (NDFs) only where a deliverable market demonstrates temporary illiquidity; otherwise prohibited for commercial treasury hedging in Canada
CAD/USD cross-currency swaps used to match long-dated institutional infrastructure project receivables
CAD/USD FX options and collars providing zero-premium conversion bands for forecasted export proceeds
Single-currency interest rate swaps solely for hedging project-completion risk, not for speculative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Service Alberta (CORES or authorized service provider)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the corporation's incorporation anniversary date; filing may be submitted up to 60 days before the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 15 late filing assessment after the anniversary date; repeated failure for two or more consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta provincial schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year end; a December 31 fiscal period is due on June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% for each complete month of delay, capped at 12 months; repeat filing failures attract a 10% penalty; interest accrues daily on amounts outstanding; prolonged non-filing can lead to deemed assessment and collection enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting or unanimous written resolution in lieu of the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal record — maintained in the corporate Minute Book; no regulatory filing is made for an ordinary private Alberta corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First annual meeting within 18 months of incorporation; each subsequent annual meeting within 15 months after the preceding annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting is an offence under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); shareholders may apply to the Court of King's Bench to call the meeting; repeated non-compliance may be cited in Registrar strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is automatically required for a private, non-distributing Alberta business corporation; the ABCA permits shareholders to waive auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder resolution. A compulsory audit applies where the corporation is a distributing or reporting issuer, where a unanimous shareholder agreement or the articles require an auditor, where the corporation has issued securities to the public, or where an order of the Alberta Court of King's Bench or a regulator requires an audit. Prudent lenders or clients may also require audited statements through private contract, but such a requirement is not a statutory corporate threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A private engineering/BIM outsourcing corporation in Alberta may prepare financial statements under Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), per the CPA Canada Handbook. ASPE is the common default for private non-listed companies; IFRS is mandatory for reporting issuers and is appropriate where lender or cross-border client contracts require IFRS. Tax reporting to CRA follows Income Tax Act rules and the elected fiscal period.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and applicable beneficial-ownership transparency rules, the corporation must maintain and retain at its registered office a Register of Individuals with Significant Control, take reasonable steps to identify all individuals with significant control, and update the register promptly after any share transfer or change in significant control. The annual return must be based on the current registered records; the director or authorized individual certifies that the register, including member and significant-control changes, is accurate as of the filing date. Alberta does not currently require a separate stand-alone annual UBO declaration fee; inspection and enforcement are carried out through the Corporate Registry and the Registrar's audit powers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings, consents, and resolutions
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 146 – USD 440 per year (CAD 200 – CAD 600) for a registered office address or Alberta corporate agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,850 – USD 14,600 per year (CAD 8,000 – CAD 20,000) for a certified audit of a small to mid-size private engineering/BIM consulting corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credit (35% refundable), Alberta manufacturing and processing tax credit

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, e-filed through CRA's My Business Account portal

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenue from CAD/BIM services, drafting fees, and related engineering activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report Canadian-source income; worldwide income if resident in Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses including salaries, software licenses, equipment depreciation for BIM modeling
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to Canadian business expenses; non-residents may claim only if carrying on business in Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion income if partial year or non-resident status

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $50 per day to a maximum of $5,000; interest on late payments; director liability for unpaid amounts

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) using Form NR301, providing DTA documentation to CRA for reduced withholding rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under DTAs; Interest: 25% statutory, reduced to 0-15% under DTAs

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 500,000 for related-party transactions requiring transfer pricing documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply where relevant activities are conducted; assessment required for Canadian tax residency and economic presence in Alberta

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Late Filing of Corporate Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission or late submission of T2 return beyond 6-month deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of $50 per day, capped at $5,000, plus accrued interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for penalties and interest; potential personal fines or disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and maintain arm's length transfer pricing documentation for intercompany transactions exceeding threshold
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustments, penalties up to 10% of adjusted amount, possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal liability including fines and imprisonment for willful evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold and remit 25% WHT on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to the withheld tax amount plus interest; possible prosecution under Income Tax Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally responsible for the tax, penalties, and interest; risk of jail time in cases of evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without sufficient economic substance in Alberta for tax residency or incentive claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to $200,000 per violation, director disqualification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for penalties; potential criminal charges and imprisonment
